title: Grammar: Adjectives agree with the noun
subtitle: Unit 4: Family and people

steps.title: Adjectives agree with the noun
steps.body: Adjectives match the gender and number of the noun. Add -e for feminine, -s for plural.

steps.title: The same -s rule: the s is silent
Adjectives agree with the noun
steps.body:
Some adjectives change more: beau → belle, vieux → vieille, gentil → gentille, blanc → blanche, roux → rousse. -e adjectives do not change in the feminine: jeune, rouge, célibataire, sympathique. Colour words used as nouns for things never change: orange, marron.

Position. Most adjectives come after the noun: une femme canadienne, un sac noir. A few short, common ones come before: grand, petit, jeune, vieux, beau, bon, mauvais, nouveau: une grande famille, un petit garçon, une belle ville.

steps.title: In Canada
steps.body: On Canadian forms: Né(e), Canadien(ne), Marié(e). The (e) tells you to add an e if you are a woman. You choose your form, you do not write both.
